title: How much less than one lakh was Chintamani?
description: A question from the book gives the population of Chintamani in twenty eleven and asks how much less it is than one lakh. The video finds the gap by taking the smaller number from the larger, and checks it by adding back.
teaching_notes: One idea: how much less means the gap, found by taking the smaller number from the larger. Ask the class to add the gap back to the smaller number and see whether one lakh returns. Watch for students who subtract in the wrong order or lose a zero in one lakh.

video_script.why: The child knows one lakh is 1,00,000 and can find a gap by subtracting.
video_script.substitution: To find how much less, take the smaller number away from the larger one.
video_script.anchor: The town of Chintamani had about seventy five thousand people: how much less than one lakh is that?
video_script.payoff_line: Seventy five thousand is twenty five thousand less than one lakh
video_script.design: One idea: how much less means the gap between two numbers. The method of the rice question is reused: compare with one lakh by subtracting. The anchor stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part; no hard clear.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>One lakh is a one followed by five zeros. We met it as the smallest six digit number.

<bookmark mark='m3'/>As with the kinds of rice, we find a gap by taking the smaller number from the larger.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, write one lakh in figures, as one followed by five zeros.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The gap is the larger number take away the smaller. That is one lakh take away seventy five thousand.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: count up in two hops: 75,000 to 80,000 is 5,000; 80,000 to 1,00,000 is 20,000

marks.m1: the first hop from 75,000 to 80,000 is drawn
marks.m2: the second hop from 80,000 to 1,00,000 is drawn

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, count up in two hops. From seventy five thousand to eighty thousand is five thousand.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>From eighty thousand to one lakh is twenty thousand.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, check by putting the hops back in the question. Seventy five thousand, plus five thousand, plus twenty thousand.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>That lands exactly on one lakh, so the hops are right.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 5,000 + 20,000 = 25,000; 75,000 is 25,000 less than one lakh
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>The two hops of five thousand and twenty thousand together make twenty five thousand.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Seventy five thousand is twenty five thousand less than one lakh.
